Rashi on Pesachim 26a:10:1.hebrew: תרומת הדשן - בכל יום היה נוטל מלא מחתה, ונותנה אצל המזבח, והיא נבלעת במקומה, כדכתיב: ״והרים את הדשן״ וגו'. ואסורה בהנאה ומועלין בה, כדכתיב: ״ושמו אצל המזבח״ — אלמא טעונה גניזה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:10:1.english: The removal of the ashes - Every day, [the priest] would take a full firepan [of ashes] and place it beside the altar, and it was swallowed up in its place, as it is written: “And he shall take up the ashes...” etc. And it is forbidden to derive benefit [from it], and it is subject to [the laws of] misuse of consecrated property, as it is written: “And he shall put it beside the altar” — which shows that it requires concealment.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:11:1.hebrew: ובגדי כהונה - ארבעה בגדי לבן שכהן גדול נכנס בהם לפני ולפנים ביום הכפורים, דאסורין שוב להשתמש בהן, כדכתיב: "והניחם שם":
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:11:1.english: And the priestly garments - The four white garments in which the High Priest enters the innermost sanctum on Yom Kippur, for they are forbidden to be used again, as it is written: “And he shall leave them there.”

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:13:1.english: This works out well according to the Rabbis - Their dispute is in Tractate Yoma (daf 24a).

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:13:2.hebrew: כשירין הם לכהן הדיוט - כל השנה, שהן הן הבגדים הראויין לשימוש הדיוט: כתונת, ומכנסים, ומצנפת, ואבנט:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:13:2.english: They are fit for a common priest - All year round, for these are the very garments suitable for use by a common priest: a tunic, trousers, a miter, and a belt.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:14:1.hebrew: עגלה ערופה - כתיב ״שם״, דמשמע: שם תהא קבורתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:14:1.english: The heifer whose neck is broken - It is written: “There,” which implies that there shall be its burial.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:15:1.hebrew: הכא מיעוטי כתיבי - בהני, למימרא דלא תיגמר מינייהו: ושמו — לזה ולא לאחר; הערופה — ולא דבר אחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:15:1.english: Here, exclusions are written - Regarding these [cases], to say that [other cases] should not be derived from them: “And he shall put it” — for this [case] and not for another; “The [heifer whose neck was] broken” — and not another matter.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:16:1.hebrew: הכניסה לרבקה - עגלה ערופה. רבקה — קופל"א (צמד) בלע"ז, שקושרין ארבע פרות ביחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:16:1.english: One brought it into a team - [This refers to] the heifer whose neck is to be broken. A rivkah is cople (a team) in Old French, where they tie four cows together.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:16:2.english: And it threshed - Grain with its companions.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:16:3.hebrew: כשירה - שלא נתכוין לכך, ולאו עבודה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:16:3.english: It is valid - Because he did not intend for this, and it is not [considered] labor.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:16:4.hebrew: ואם נתכוין שתינק ותדוש פסולה - והכא לא אפשר שלא יכניסנה שתינק, וכי מתכוין שתינק ותידוש — פסולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:16:4.english: And if he intended that it nurse and thresh, it is disqualified - And here, it is impossible not to bring it in so that it may nurse, and when he intends that it nurse and thresh, it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:17:1.hebrew: אשר לא עובד בה מכל מקום - דאע"ג דבעלמא לא מיתסר, הכא אסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:17:1.english: “Which has not been worked with” in any case - That even though in general it is not forbidden, here it is forbidden.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:1:1.hebrew: ורבא אמר לן עד כאן - לא שמעת ליה לרבי יהודה דלא אזיל בתר כוונה, אלא דלא פטר ליה משום אין מתכוין בדאפשר — דמתכוין אסור לדברי הכל — ומשוי שאין מיכוין כמתכוין לחומרא לאסור. אבל דלא חשיבא ליה כוונה, דמשוי מכוין כשאין מתכוין לקולא — כגון דלא אפשר, בשאין מתכוין שרי, ונישרי נמי רבי יהודה במתכוין דלא חשיב כוונה כלל — הא לא שמעת ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:1:1.english: And Rava said to us: Up to this point - You have not heard of Rabbi Yehuda that he does not follow intention, except that he did not exempt him on account of [a lack of] intent where [avoiding] is possible — for [acting with] intent is forbidden according to all — and he treats one who does not intend like one who intends, as a stringency, to forbid [it]. But that intention is of no significance to him, such that he would treat one who intends like one who does not intend, as a leniency — such as where it is not possible [to avoid], where when one does not intend it is permitted, and [so] let Rabbi Yehuda also permit [when] one intends, because he does not consider intention at all — that you have not heard of him.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:2:1.hebrew: ההיכל - גובהו מאה אמה, וצילו הולך למרחוק מאד ברחוב שלפני הר הבית. ומתוך שרחוב גדול היה ומחזיק בני אדם הרבה, היה דורש שם מפני החמה, שאין לך בית המדרש מחזיקן:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:2:1.english: The Sanctuary - Its height was one hundred cubits, and its shadow extended very far into the plaza in front of the Temple Mount. And since it was a large plaza and [could] hold many people, he would expound there [in its shade] on account of the sun, for there is no study hall that [could] hold them.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:2:2.english: Where it was not possible - [To refrain] from expounding to the public the laws of the Festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:3:1.hebrew: דלתוכו עשוי - ואין הנאת צילו נאסרה, דאין זה דרך הנאתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:3:1.english: As it was constructed for its interior - And the benefit of its shade is not forbidden, for this is not the manner of its benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:4:1.hebrew: לול - ארובה שבעלייה היורדת לבית, קרי לול:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:4:1.english: An opening - An aperture in the upper chamber that descends into the house, [the Tanna] calls a lul.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:4:2.english: The artisans - When there is damage in the wall of the Holy of Holies.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:4:3.hebrew: יזונו - לשון הנאה, כמזונות, שמשביע עצמו ממראית נוי המלאכה ונהנה:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:4:3.english: They will feast - An expression of pleasure, like sustenance, in that one sates himself from the sight of the beauty of the craftsmanship and derives pleasure.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:4:4.hebrew: והא הכא דלא אפשר - שלא ירדו לתקן, ואפילו הכי צריך לתת אותן בתיבות, שלא יוכלו להסתכל אנה ואנה, דילמא מיכווני ליהנות, ואסור:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:4:4.english: And behold, here, where it is impossible - That they not go down to repair; and even so, it is necessary to place them in boxes so that they will not be able to look here and there, lest they intend to derive benefit, and it is forbidden.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:5:1.english: Sound - Of musical instruments that are consecrated property.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:5:3.hebrew: אין בהן משום מעילה - דאורייתא, הואיל ואין בהם ממש. וכיון דמדאורייתא שרו, כי לא אפשר כגון הכא — אמאי אטרחינהו רבנן? אלא מעלה בעלמא הואי:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:5:3.english: Are not subject to [the prohibition of] misuse - [This means] by Torah law, since they have no [tangible] substance. And since by Torah law they are permitted, when it is impossible [to avoid], such as here — why would the Rabbis burden them? Rather, it was merely a higher standard.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:6:1.hebrew: קול ומראה - אין בהם ממש, ופטור לעולם:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:6:1.english: Sound and sight - They have no substance, and [one is] always exempt [from misuse]:

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:6:2.hebrew: וריח - יש בו ממש בסממנין, לפיכך חייב. ודקא אמר רבי יהושע פטור — לאחר שתעלה תמרתו במקדש קאמר, דמשום דנעשית מצותו ואין צורך גבוה עוד בה, יצתה מכלל קדשי ה'. וברייתא — במריח בה בביתו, שנותן ממנה על הגחלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:6:2.english: And smell - There is [tangible] substance in the spices; therefore, [fundamentally,] one is liable [for misuse of consecrated property]. And as for that which Rabbi Yehoshua said, [that one is] exempt — he was speaking of [smelling it] after its column of smoke ascends in the Temple, for since its mitzvah has been performed and the Most High has no further need for it, it has exited the category of "the sacred things of the Lord." And the baraita [which states that one has committed misuse] is [referring to] one who smells it in his home, who places some of it upon the coals.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:7:1.hebrew: העומדים בפנים - לשמש, דלא אפשר מלעמוד שם, ואסור להו להיות מתכוונים:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:7:1.english: Those standing inside - To perform the [Temple] service, as it is not possible [to avoid] standing there, and it is prohibited for them to intend [to derive benefit].

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:7:2.hebrew: לאותן העומדים בחוץ - קאמר: אין מעילה, הא איסורא איכא. אבל לעומדין בפנים, אפילו איסורא ליכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:7:2.english: To those standing outside - It states: "There is no [liability for] misuse of consecrated property, but there is a prohibition"; but for those standing inside, there is not even a prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:8:1.english: One who compounds the incense - [This refers to] unauthorized incense that does not belong to the community.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:8:2.hebrew: אם להתלמד בה או למוסרה - אחר פיטומה לציבור, פטור מכרת. אבל אם דעתו להצניע לצורכו להריח בה, ועשאה בסממנין הכתובים — חייב כרת, דכתיב (שמות ל), איש אשר יעשה כמוה להריח בה ונכרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:8:2.english: If to learn with it or to transfer it - [To transfer it] after its compounding to the community — [he is] exempt from karet. But if his intention was to store [it] away for his own need in order to smell it, and he prepared it with the prescribed ingredients — he is liable to karet, as it is written (Exodus 30:38): “A man who shall make [any] like it, to smell it, shall be cut off [from his people].”

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:8:3.hebrew: והמריח בה - בקטורת של ציבור, פטור מכרת ומחטאת, דלא חייבה תורה אלא מפטם להריח:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:8:3.english: And one who smells it - [With regard to] communal incense, [he is] exempt from karet and from a sin-offering, for the Torah held liable only [one who] compounds [it] to smell [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:9:1.hebrew: אין בהן משום מעילה - דאורייתא, הואיל ואין בהם ממש. וכיון דמדאורייתא שרו, כי לא אפשר כגון הכא — אמאי אטרחינהו רבנן? אלא מעלה בעלמא הואי:
Rashi on Pesachim 26a:9:1.english: [They] are not subject to misuse of consecrated property - [This is] by Torah law, since they have no substance. And since by Torah law they are permitted, when it is impossible [to avoid], such as here, why did the Rabbis trouble them? Rather, it was merely an extra stringency.

Rashi on Pesachim 26a:9:2.english: Its column of smoke - The column of its smoke.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:15:1.hebrew: כתיב הכא ושמו וכתיב התם הערופה - תימה לר"י: אמאי איצטריך תרי מיעוטי? בחד סגי, דלהכי כתביה — דלא למילף מינייהו! וי"ל: דאי לא כתיב אלא חד מיעוטא, לא הוה מצי למעוטי אלא מילתא דלא דמי כל כך למיסר, אבל מילתא דדמי למיסר — לא; להכי איצטריך תרווייהו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:15:1.english: It is written here: “And he shall put it,” and it is written there: “The heifer whose neck is broken” - The Ri is astounded: Why was it necessary [to have] two exclusions? One would suffice, for that is why [the verse] wrote it — so that [other cases] should not be derived from them! And one can say: Had only one exclusion been written, it would only have been able to exclude a matter that is not so similar [so as] to forbid [it], but a matter that is similar [so as] to forbid [it], [it would] not [exclude]. Therefore, both of them were necessary.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:16:1.english: "If one brought it into a cow pen" - In the Tosefta it is taught regarding the [red] heifer.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:3:1.hebrew: שאני היכל דלתוכו עשוי - פ"ה: ואין הנאת צילו נאסרת, שאין זה דרך הנאתו. וא"ת: והא לא כתיב אכילה, ואפילו שלא כדרך הנאה יהא אסור? וי"ל: דמעילה ילפינן "חטא" "חטא" מתרומה, ובתרומה כתיב אכילה. והא דאסר בפ' כל הצלמים (ע"ז מח:) לישב תחת אשירה — משום דאשירה לצל עשויה, והיא דרך הנאה; ועוד, דגבי ע"ז לא כתיב אכילה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:3:1.english: "The Sanctuary is different, as it was constructed for its interior" - Rashi explained: And the benefit of its shade is not forbidden, because this is not the [customary] manner of its benefit. And if you will say: But "eating" is not written [regarding consecrated property], and [therefore] even not in the customary manner of benefit it should be forbidden? And one can say: That regarding me'ilah [misuse of consecrated property], we derive [by a verbal analogy of] "sin" [and] "sin" from terumah, and regarding terumah, "eating" is written. And as for that which [the Mishnah] prohibits in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaTzelamim (Avodah Zarah 48b) to sit beneath an asherah [tree] — [that is] because an asherah was made for shade, and [so sitting beneath it] is the customary manner of benefit; and furthermore, regarding idolatry, "eating" is not written.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:4:1.hebrew: והא הכא דלא אפשר וקמיכוין ואסור - ה"מ אביי לאוקמא כרבי שמעון, דאליבא דרבי יהודה פליגי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:4:1.english: And here, where it is not possible and he intends, it is prohibited - Abaye could have established [the baraita] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, as they dispute [only] according to Rabbi Yehudah.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:5:1.hebrew: ותסברא והאמר רבי שמעון בן פזי קול ומראה וריח אין בהן משום מעילה - פ"ה: וכיון דמדאורייתא שרי, כי לא אפשר — אמאי אטרחוה רבנן? וקשה לר"י: הא בגרירה, דליכא איסורא דאורייתא, ופליג רבא ואסר בלא אפשר ומיכוון, ומאי קא מוכיח אביי לרבא? וי"ל דה"פ: כיון דלא אסירי אלא מדרבנן, א"כ כשהוא לצורך, כגון לתקן בית קדשי הקדשים — סברא הוא דאפילו איסורא דרבנן ליכא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:5:1.english: "And can you understand [this]?! But didn't Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi say: Sound, sight, and smell are not subject to [the prohibition of] misuse" - Rashi explained: And since by Torah law it is permitted, when it is impossible [to avoid], why would the Rabbis have burdened them? And the Ri finds this difficult: For in [the case of] dragging, where there is no Torah prohibition, yet Rava disagrees and prohibits [even] when it is impossible [to avoid] and he intends; and [if so,] what did Abaye prove to Rava? And one can say that this is what it means: Since they are prohibited only rabbinically, if so, when it is for a need, such as to repair the Holy of Holies, it stands to reason that there is not even a rabbinic prohibition.

Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:6:1.hebrew: מעילה הוא דליכא הא איסורא איכא - תימה, דבפרק החליל (סוכה נג. ושם) תניא: אשה בוררת חטים לאור של בית השואבה; והשמן והפתילה היו של קודש, כדתנן התם. ובירושלמי דייק מינה דקול ומראה וריח אין בהן משום מעילה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:6:1.english: It is [only] me'ilah that is not [incurred], but a prohibition exists - [This is] puzzling, for in the chapter [entitled] Hechalil (Sukkah 53a, and there), it is taught: "A woman would sift wheat by the light of the Beit HaSho'evah"; and the oil and the wick were consecrated, as we learned there [in the Mishnah]. And in the Yerushalmi, [the Gemara] infers from this that sound, sight, and smell are not subject to [the prohibition of] me'ilah [implying that no prohibition applies at all].

Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:7:1.hebrew: לאותן העומדים בחוץ - ליכא איסורא, אלא שלא יקרבו עצמן לעזרה כדי להריח יותר; דהא אמרינן (יומא דף לח:): "לא היתה כלה צריכה להתבשם בירושלים מפני ריח הקטורת":
Tosafot on Pesachim 26a:7:1.english: "To those standing outside" - There is no prohibition [in general], except that they should not bring themselves closer to the Courtyard in order to smell [it] more, for we say (Yoma 38b): "A bride in Jerusalem did not need to perfume herself because of the fragrance of the incense."
